answers.rationale: A Monday-morning crate check requires being locally available before the workday begins, so Sunday arrival is the proportionate schedule buffer. The lifeline shows that arrival timing changes with setup and access constraints rather than reflecting a fixed preference for arriving a set number of days early.

With the first required work block not until Tuesday afternoon and only an informal Monday dinner, Monday arrival and one hotel night is sufficient. There is no operational reason in the prompt to add a Sunday night or force a Tuesday-dawn arrival.

The kit is already staged and the first assigned block is late Wednesday afternoon, so a Wednesday-morning arrival is the calibrated, non-excessive plan. Prior trips show earlier arrivals were used when setup, crate handling, or early access actually required them; they do not support a fixed night-before-arrival preference.

For a user-forum badge-scanner box, the booth/show decorator is the operationally appropriate receiver because the item is intended for the event rather than a hotel, branch, or plant. Receiver selection is context-dependent in the lifeline: small conference items have gone to hotels, equipment to distributor sites, and exhibit materials to decorators. Final shipment should still depend on decorator acceptance and labeling instructions, which are not stated here.
